prompt: A brief you absorbed (Brief D) contains an internal-links-in line pointing to a follow-up brief that does not exist yet. When do you write it?
chosen: Next run, one brief per run, before the referenced link dangles for days. The follow-up is part of the delivered artifact's integrity, not a nice-to-have. Name it as the next candidate so the queue survives compaction.
rejected: Leave it in the gaps list indefinitely; the writer can chase the reference if they care.

prompt: How do you keep the follow-up brief from becoming a thin duplicate of its parent?
chosen: Give it a different intent and a different target query: parent Brief D is a software tutorial (MAXQDA, how-to), Brief G is a decision guide (saturation, when-to-stop). Bidirectional internal links serve navigation, not keyword duplication; the one-owner-per-topic map still holds one topic per site.
rejected: Reuse the parent's structure with the query swapped in, since both live on kanoon-research.ir.

prompt: Brief D's verify-before-drafting gate was about software versions and screenshots. Does it apply to a methodological follow-up?
chosen: The gate survives; only the object changes: verify cited-paper figures (Guest et al. 2006 numbers and conditions) from the paper itself before quoting, and any cited university guidance. The discipline is 'verify the claim's source', not 'check software menus'.
rejected: Methodological concepts don't need verification gates — only software facts do.

prompt: The brief title is 55 characters against the 60-char house limit. What do you owe the record?
chosen: Record the exact count in the brief ('55 chars — counted') so the writer doesn't have to recount. Never claim a count you haven't run; if the count had landed over 60, provide a shorter option instead of hoping nobody checks.
rejected: Skip the count — the title looks short enough.

prompt: Brief G was written without any new post from the writer lane. Does it need a room update?
chosen: No. Absorbed briefs live as files; corrections went to the issue thread because they edit already-posted drafts. Post to the room only when the batch needs a lane decision — a new file no lane is waiting on is noise. The reconciliation read records coverage.
rejected: Post every new brief to the issue thread so the team sees progress.

prompt: After closing reconciliation gap 1 with Brief G, where do the remaining brief candidates go?
chosen: Name them in the batch-status section of the new brief (the ideas-board P1s), so the next run inherits the exact queue: teznevise stats-test hub, tezagah Fluent-divergence, and the rest. One per run, per the staged pace.
rejected: Rely on the reconciliation report as the queue — the brief doesn't need to repeat it.
